deed: Aaron Lopez founded a spermaceti candle factory in Newport and became the city's wealthiest resident
title: Aaron Lopez, a Jewish merchant in Newport, opened a spermaceti candle factory in 1756 and became the city's wealthiest man

trailer.text: According to Edward Howe, Aaron Lopez (1731–1782), a Sephardic Jew, became the wealthiest merchant in colonial Newport.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he was born in Portugal, went to Newport in 1752, and there renounced his Marrano past.
According to Howe, in 1756 Lopez opened a spermaceti candle factory in Newport; spermaceti is a waxy substance extracted from whale oil.
According to the Newport Historical Society, he owned businesses refining whale oil and sugar into candles and rum, and sold them in the city's marketplace.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, the people of Newport mourned him; he had contributed greatly to their prosperity before the Revolution.

paragraphs.text: Aaron Lopez grew up in Portugal and practiced Judaism in secret, while outwardly maintaining an appearance of loyalty to Catholicism.
Outwardly, he conformed to Christianity.
According to the University of Miami, he was a Jewish merchant of Portuguese converso origin.
With him came his wife Anna, his daughter Catherine and his brother David.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, in Newport he renounced his Marrano past, remarried in a Jewish ceremony and underwent circumcision.
According to the Newport Historical Society, there the family openly embraced the Jewish faith, which was outlawed in Portugal.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Aaron Lopez (1731–1782) was born in Portugal and came to Newport, Rhode Island, in 1752.
According to the Jewish Press, Jews were pioneers in the spermaceti candle business in colonial America.
According to the Jewish Press, in 1751 Rivera began to purchase “head matter” from the whale's head, and developed a method for separating the oil from the spermaceti.
According to Edward Howe, in 1756 Lopez opened a candle factory in Newport that relied on spermaceti, a waxy substance extracted from whale oil.

According to an article by Dr. Yitzchak Levine, quoting an archival reference page on the cjh.org website, one of Lopez's early ventures was participation in a consortium of Newport merchants for the manufacture of spermaceti candles.
According to the Newport Historical Society, Lopez owned several businesses on land, primarily refining whale oil and sugar into candles and rum.
According to the same source, he sold them in Newport's marketplace.
According to My Jewish Learning, the family was engaged in shipping, whaling and candle manufacturing.
According to Howe, when the price of whale oil soared, Lopez joined a trust called the United Company of Spermaceti Chandlers in 1761.
According to Howe, the aim of the trust was to control price and distribution among its members.
According to the Jewish Press, Rivera, Lopez and Isaac Hart signed an agreement on November 5, 1761.
According to the same source, the agreement set a maximum price for the large supplier of head matter and a price for the sale of candles throughout New England.
According to the Jewish Press, the agreement is considered the first attempt in American history to restrain trade through anti-competitive collaboration.
On April 13, 1763, an agreement for the manufacture of spermaceti candles was signed in Newport.
Among the ten signatories were four Jews, including Aaron Lopez and Moses Lopez.
According to Jewish Currents, the agreement bound the manufacturers to pay a maximum price per ton of whale head matter.
According to the same source, the agreement also bound them to prevent, by every fair means, new competitors from entering the trade.
According to the Jewish Press, between 1760 and 1776 Lopez dispatched well over 200 voyages from Newport.
According to the Newport Historical Society, at the start of 1775 Lopez owned more than thirty trading ships and ran profitable candle-making and distilling operations.
According to the same source, he owned assets worth thousands of pounds sterling.
According to tax records, in the early 1770s Lopez was Newport's wealthiest resident.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, on the eve of the American Revolution he was the city's leading merchant and its largest taxpayer.
According to the Jewish Press, he was called “The Merchant Prince of New England.”
According to the same source, he is credited with the leading role in Newport's rapid commercial development.
According to the Newport Historical Society, Lopez joined a thriving Jewish community in Newport.
According to the same source, in the early 1760s he helped fund the construction of a synagogue.
According to Dr. Yitzchok Levine, Lopez played a key role in establishing the synagogue that later became known as the Touro Synagogue.
According to the Loeb website, he had the honor of laying the cornerstone when construction began.
According to the Jewish Press, Lopez was meticulous about the Sabbath and festivals, and did not permit his employees to work on these days, even on minor holidays.
According to JTA, Lopez prohibited ships from departing from his dock on both the Jewish and the Christian Sabbath.
Lopez donated lumber for the construction of the College of Rhode Island, which later became Brown University.
According to the Newport Historical Society, Jews could not be citizens of the colony of Rhode Island, because they were not Christians.
According to the same source, they were barred from voting, holding office and serving in the militia.
According to the Loeb website, the Rhode Island Superior Court denied the citizenship requests of Lopez and of another Jew, Isaac Elizer.
According to the Jewish Press, the ruling stated that under the colony's charter and under a law of 1663, anyone who did not profess the Christian religion could not be admitted as a freeman.
According to the Jewish Press, on October 15, 1762 Lopez was recognized as a citizen in Massachusetts, and was the first Jew to be naturalized in that colony.
According to the Newport Historical Society, in 1775 Lopez's candle workshops could not operate without a steady supply of whale oil.
According to the same source, his distilleries lay idle without sugar.
According to the Newport Historical Society, in the mobilization of the spring and summer of 1775 his businesses lost employees, and his ships lost sailors.
According to the same source, as a prominent citizen he was expected to aid hundreds of his employees, clients and members of the Jewish community who were in distress.
According to the Newport Historical Society, the boycott had already cut into profits, and the outbreak of war brought an almost total cessation of most trade through Newport.
According to the same source, by the end of 1775 the Lopez family was near bankruptcy.

According to the Newport Historical Society, Lopez, who also cultivated ties with British officials, ultimately chose to side with the Patriots, and this decision put him at odds with many members of his Jewish community in Newport who became Loyalists.
According to the same source, after the move to Taunton Lopez began to rebuild his businesses.
According to the Society, he did so by supplying clothing and food to the Continental Army and by investing in privateers.
According to the Jewish Press, he was an important supplier of munitions to the American forces, and equipped ships of his own with guns to serve as armed frigates.
According to the Jewish Press, in Leicester Lopez, together with Rivera and 70 members of Newport's Jewish community, founded the first Jewish community in Massachusetts.

stations.title: His death and the city's mourning

paragraphs.text: In 1782 Lopez drowned in a pond.
According to JTA, he left a wife and 15 children.
According to the Jewish Press, Lopez was buried in the Jewish cemetery in Newport.
According to the same source, not only the Jewish community mourned him, but all the people of Newport.
According to My Jewish Learning, Yale president Ezra Stiles, on hearing of his death, wrote that he was an “amiable, benevolent, most hospitable & very respectable gentleman”.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Stiles wrote of a “demonstration of universal sorrow.”
According to Howe, Lopez engaged in the slave trade between 1761 and 1774, although it was only a small part of his business.
According to the Newport Historical Society, Lopez transported whale oil, sugar and enslaved people across the Atlantic.
According to the Jewish Press, Lopez and Rivera sent 14 slave ships to the west coast of Africa between 1761 and 1774.
According to an estimate in the same source, their ships brought more than 1,100 slaves from West Africa to the West Indies and the southern colonies.
According to the Jewish Press, Lopez owned five slaves and Rivera owned twelve.
According to the same source, they used the slaves in the hard work of rendering the whales' head matter for making candles.
According to the Jewish Press, there is evidence that few of the slaving voyages turned a profit, and overall their involvement in them resulted in a net loss for Lopez and Rivera.

disagreements.question: When did the family leave Portugal, and where did it go?

versions.says: According to My Jewish Learning, the Lopez family left Portugal for New York in 1740
According to Dr. Yitzchok Levine, Lopez arrived in Newport on October 13, 1752

disagreements.question: When did the manufacture of candles from whale head matter begin in America?

versions.says: According to the Nantucket Historical Association, manufacture began around 1748
According to the Jewish Press, Rivera began purchasing head matter for candle making in 1751

disagreements.question: How many ships did Lopez own?

versions.says: According to the Jewish Press, more than 120 ships, including about thirty ocean-going vessels
According to Howe, more than 30 sailing vessels, in full or part ownership
According to JTA, part ownership of more than 30 ocean-going ships and more than 100 coastal vessels

disagreements.question: How much lumber was donated to the College of Rhode Island?

versions.says: According to Howe, Lopez donated 5,000 feet of lumber in 1764
According to the Jewish Press, Rivera and Lopez together donated 10,000 feet of lumber

disagreements.question: Why was the citizenship application in Rhode Island rejected?

versions.says: According to the Jewish Press, the Rhode Island Superior Court rejected the application in March 1762 on the spurious grounds that the Act was designed to increase the colony's population and that it already had enough inhabitants, but the real reason was open antisemitism.

According to My Jewish Learning, there is no official record of the reasons why the Rhode Island Superior Court first turned down the naturalization application of Lopez and Elizer, but at the rehearing in March 1762 the court justified the rejection on the grounds that the colony was already crowded and that, under a law of 1663, anyone who does not profess the Christian religion cannot be admitted as a freeman.

disagreements.question: Where was Lopez granted citizenship in Massachusetts?

versions.says: According to Howe, in Swansea, on October 15, 1762
According to My Jewish Learning, at a court session in Taunton in October 1762, to which he came with a certificate from the deputy governor of Rhode Island

disagreements.question: Where did Lopez move during the war, and when?

versions.says: According to the Newport Historical Society, he moved to Taunton, Massachusetts, in early 1776
According to Howe, the British occupation of Newport in 1776 forced him and his family to move to Leicester
According to Dr. Yitzchok Levine, in Leicester Lopez set up a retail shop and a modest commodities trade
According to Howe, on May 28, 1782 his horse and carriage swerved into Scott’s Pond in Smithfield, Rhode Island, as he was on his way back to Newport
According to JTA, he drowned in a pond while watering his horse

unknowns.text: The page does not know exactly how many people worked in the candle factory. The Newport Historical Society speaks of hundreds, but that number includes employees, clients and community members together
The thriving Jewish community in Newport that Lopez joined numbered around a dozen families.

claims.text: לפי אגודת ניופורט ההיסטורית, פרוץ המלחמה הביא להפסקה כמעט מוחלטת של רוב הסחר דרך ניופורט, אחרי שהחרם כבר פגע ברווחים.
claims.quote: The boycott had already cut into profits, and the outbreak of war led to a total cessation of most trade through Newport.

claims.text: לפי אגודת ניופורט ההיסטורית, עד סוף 1775 הייתה משפחת לופז קרובה לפשיטת רגל.
claims.quote: Even if they retained some assets overseas, by the end of the year, the Lopez family was near bankruptcy.

claims.text: לפי אגודת ניופורט ההיסטורית, לופז היה נאמן לגורם הפטריוטי למרות התנגדות רבים מקהילתו היהודית בניופורט שהפכו ללויאליסטים.
claims.quote: Aaron Lopez’s decision to side with the Patriots put him at odds with many members of Newport’s Jewish community

claims.text: לפי אגודת ניופורט ההיסטורית, אחרי המעבר לטאונטון שבמסצ'וסטס בתחילת 1776 החל לופז לשקם את האימפריה שלו באספקת ביגוד ומזון לצבא הקונטיננטלי ובהשקעה בספינות קורסיר.
claims.quote: After moving to Taunton, Massachusetts in early 1776, Lopez began to rebuild his empire by supplying clothing and provisions to the Continental Army and investing in New England privateers.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, לופז היה ספק חשוב של תחמושת לכוחות האמריקנים, וצייד ספינות משלו בתותחים כדי לשמש כפריגטות חמושות.
claims.quote: used the proceeds from his business to become an important supplier of munitions to American forces, including equipping his own ships with guns to serve as armed frigates

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, בלסטר הקים לופז יחד עם ריברה, עם 70 מחברי הקהילה היהודית של ניופורט, את הקהילה היהודית הראשונה במסצ'וסטס.
claims.quote: He relocated to Leicester where, together with Rivera, he took 70 members of the Newport Jewish community and founded the first Jewish community in Massachusetts.

claims.text: לפי האו, ב-28 במאי 1782 טבע לופז כשסוסו ועגלתו סטו אל תוך בריכת סקוט בסמית'פילד שברוד איילנד, בדרכו חזרה לניופורט.
claims.quote: Unfortunately, on May 28, 1782 Lopez drowned when his horse and carriage swerved into Scott’s Pond in Smithfield, R.I.

claims.text: לפי JTA, לופז מת ב-1782 בטביעה בבריכה בזמן שהשקה את סוסו, והותיר אישה ו-15 ילדים.
claims.quote: Lopez died in 1782 by drowning in a pond while watering his horse; he left behind a wife and 15 children.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, לופז נקבר בבית הקברות היהודי בניופורט ונקבר באבל לא רק בידי הקהילה היהודית אלא בידי כל תושבי ניופורט.
claims.quote: He was buried in the Jewish cemetery in Newport and was mourned not only by the Jewish community but by all Newporters.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, כששמע נשיא ייל, עזרא סטיילס, על מות לופז כתב שהיה 'ג'נטלמן חביב, נדיב, מכניס אורחים ומכובד מאוד'.
claims.quote: On hearing of Lopez’s death, president Ezra Stiles of Yale College wrote that Lopez was an “amiable, benevolent, most hospitable & very respectable gentleman

claims.text: לפי האו, לופז עסק בסחר בעבדים בין 1761 ל-1774, אף שזה היה חלק קטן בלבד מעסקיו.
claims.quote: Although only a small part of his mercantile business, Lopez engaged in the slave trade between 1761 and 1774.

claims.text: לפי אגודת ניופורט ההיסטורית, לופז הוביל בים האטלנטי שמן לווייתנים, סוכר ובני אדם משועבדים.
claims.quote: Now going by Aaron, Lopez transported whale oil, sugar, and enslaved people across the Atlantic.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, לופז וריברה שלחו 14 ספינות עבדים לחוף המערבי של אפריקה בין 1761 ל-1774.
claims.quote: Lopez’s (and Rivera’s) involvement in the slave trade included sending 14 slave ships to the west coast of Africa between 1761 and 1774

claims.text: לפי הערכה ב-Jewish Press, ספינותיהם של לופז וריברה הביאו יותר מ-1,100 עבדים ממערב אפריקה לאיי הודו המערבית ולמושבות הדרומיות.
claims.quote: Over that fourteen-year period, it is estimated that their ships brought over 1,100 slaves from West Africa to the West Indies and the southern colonies of America.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, לופז החזיק חמישה עבדים וריברה שנים עשר, והשתמשו בהם בעבודה הקשה של עיבוד חומר הראש של הלוויתנים לייצור נרות.
claims.quote: Lopez personally owned five slaves and Rivera twelve, and they used their slaves in the difficult and unpleasant work of rendering the whale head matter for making candles.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, יש עדויות שמעט ממסעות העבדים הניבו רווח, ובסך הכול העיסוק בהם הסב ללופז ולריברה הפסד נקי.
claims.quote: there is evidence that few of them turned a profit and, in general, the slaving enterprise resulted in a net loss for Lopez and Rivera.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, משפחת לופז עזבה את פורטוגל לניו יורק ב-1740 אחרי שחיה כאנוסים.
claims.quote: The Lopez family left Portugal for New York in 1740.

claims.text: לפי ד"ר יצחק לוין, לופז הגיע לניופורט ב-13 באוקטובר 1752 ומיד אימץ את החופש החדש לחיות כיהודי.
claims.quote: Arriving in Newport (on October 13, 1752) the Lopezes lost no time in availing themselves of their new freedom.

claims.text: לפי האגודה ההיסטורית של נאנטקט, ייצור נרות מחומר ראש של לוויתני זרע החל באמריקה בסביבות 1748.
claims.quote: The art of manufacturing candles from the headmatter of sperm whales began in America around 1748.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, עד 1770 היה לופז לאיש העשיר ביותר בניופורט, והחזיק מזח ויותר מ-120 ספינות, בהן כשלושים ספינות אוקיינוס.
claims.quote: He owned a wharf and over 120 ships, including some thirty transoceanic vessels for European and West Indies trade, which he built, chartered, and outfitted

claims.text: לפי האו, עד המהפכה האמריקנית היו ללופז בעלות מלאה או חלקית על יותר מ-30 כלי שיט.
claims.quote: As his trading activity thrived up to the American Revolution, he had full or part ownership of more than 30 sailing vessels of varying kinds.

claims.text: לפי JTA, נאמר שללופז היה לפחות חלק בבעלות על יותר מ-30 ספינות אוקיינוס ויותר מ-100 כלי שיט חופיים.
claims.quote: Lopez was said to have had at least partial ownership of over 30 transoceanic ships and more than 100 coastal vessels.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Press, בית המשפט העליון של רוד איילנד דחה את בקשת האזרחות של לופז במרץ 1762 בנימוק שהחוק נועד להגדיל את האוכלוסייה והמושבה כבר מלאה בתושבים.
claims.quote: However, his application was rejected by the Rhode Island Superior Court in March 1762 on the spurious basis that the Act was designed to increase the population of the colony

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, אין תיעוד רשמי לסיבות שבגללן דחה בית המשפט העליון של רוד איילנד את בקשת הנתינות של לופז ואליזר.
claims.quote: There is no official record of the reasons why the Rhode Island Superior Court turned down Aaron Lopez and Isaac Elizer’s naturalization application

claims.text: לפי האו, לופז הפך לאזרח ב-15 באוקטובר 1762 בסוונסי שבמסצ'וסטס.
claims.quote: On Oct. 15, 1762 he became a naturalized citizen in Swansea, Mass. He was the first Jew granted this certificate in that colony.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, באוקטובר 1762 הופיע לופז בישיבת בית משפט בטאונטון שבמסצ'וסטס עם תעודה מסגן המושל של רוד איילנד, ושם אושרה נתינותו.
claims.quote: Aaron Lopez appeared at a court session in Taunton, Massachusetts with a certificate from the deputy governor of Rhode Island

claims.text: לפי האו, כיבוש ניופורט בידי הבריטים ב-1776 אילץ את לופז ומשפחתו לעבור ללסטר.
claims.quote: The resulting British occupation of Newport in 1776 forced Lopez and his family to relocate to Leicester.

claims.text: לפי ד"ר יצחק לוין, כשהבריטים כבשו את סוואנה ב-1778 פינה לופז את משפחתו ללסטר שבמסצ'וסטס, ושם הקים חנות קמעונאית וסחר צנוע בסחורות.
claims.quote: As the British took Savannah in 1778, Lopez evacuated his family to Leicester, Massachusetts, where he set up a retail shop and a modest commodities trade

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית (Encyclopaedia Judaica), אהרן לופז (1731–1782) נולד בפורטוגל, והגיע ב-1752 לניופורט שברוד איילנד.
claims.quote: (1731–1782), American merchant-shipper. Born in Portugal, Lopez went in 1752 to Newport, Rhode Island
